fix.quote: join People’s March to Reclaim Democracy on 23rd October 2026
fix.note: The alliance's release as republished by Countercurrents (byline 18 October 2026, released by the Media Wing, PA-SIR All India Coordination Committee). The formation date of 14 October is from Business Today and Hindustan Times, not from the release. Read 22 October 2026. No time or Delhi assembly point from the organisers, and no cancellation or police refusal, had been reported by 22 October. The release says the march will not request police permission anywhere.

checked.note: Opened the Countercurrents page (curl, 200). Title, organiser, date, place (district/tehsil headquarters, state and national capital) and kind are supported. The quote is not character for character: the source uses a curly apostrophe in People’s. The release does not give the alliance's formation date. Business Today (22 Oct, 8:30 am) and India Today (21 Oct) say it was formed on 14 October, and Hindustan Times (14 Oct) says it was formed that Wednesday and its statement was issued from Surjeet Bhavan. The countercurrents author page for People Against SIR holds only this one post. No organiser update with a time or a Delhi assembly point was found, and no report of cancellation or police refusal by 22 October. Business Today and India Today say the alliance invited INDIA bloc parties and their participation was not confirmed. Deccan Chronicle (21 Oct) headlines it as People Against SIR and the INDIA bloc holding the march, but its text says only that the alliance called on the INDIA bloc for support. Deccan Herald also names a CPI(ML)L leader among the coalition's speakers. The organiser remains a civil-society alliance, so it stays in scope, but the caller may want to watch for party co-sponsorship.

fix.note: The Commission's press release of 14 October 2026, hosted by LiveLaw. PTI's report of 15 October (via ThePrint) confirms the hearing took place, heard by Justices Patnaik, Sharma and Prakash. Justice Lokur did not attend. Read 22 October 2026. Further releases are at lafc.in/press-releases, which did not list a later hearing on 22 October.

checked.note: Opened the LiveLaw PDF (pdftotext). Title, organiser, date, time (9:00 AM to 1:30 PM), kind and quote (verbatim) confirmed. The venue line reads 'Jawahar Bhawan, Dr Rajendra Prasad Road, Windsor Place, New Delhi'. source_kind organiser is right (the Commission's own release, issued by its Secretariat, hosted by LiveLaw). The release is an announcement and cannot itself support the past-tense 'Voters gave testimony'. PTI on ThePrint (15 Oct) supports it: retired judges Patnaik, Rekha Sharma and Anjana Prakash heard accounts from voters in West Bengal, Delhi, Telangana, Bihar and Rajasthan, and Lokur could not attend. Hindustan Times (14 Oct) described it as a closed-door, in-camera hearing, while the release calls it a public hearing. lafc.in/press-releases lists releases up to 9 October and no later hearing. The LAFC release of 2 October says regional benches will hold hearings across the country, with a report by December 2026, but gives no dates. A Media Coordinator's phone number appears in both releases and is not recorded here.

fix.what: A public hearing on a door-to-door audit of the roll in two polling booths. More than 150 voters registered to put their cases to a panel of advocates and activists.
fix.note: The Hindu, published 18 October 2026 and updated 19 October. The Indian Express and NewsBytes give the same date and organisers. The two papers give different sizes for the audit, 258 households in The Hindu and 307 households with 1,579 voters in The Indian Express. Read 22 October 2026.

checked.note: NewsBytes returned 403 to curl and was read through Firecrawl. It is dated 18 Oct and its quote is verbatim. The Hindu's own report was opened directly (curl, 200): 'Delhi SIR: Public audit in two booths finds over 100 voters wrongly marked absent, shifted, or dead', published 18 Oct 2026 10:16 pm, updated 19 Oct 5:40 pm. It says the Jan Sunwai was held in the Batla House area on Sunday (October 18, 2026), organised by Jan Sarokar, MKSS, Voter Adhikar Manch and NFIW, for residents of G and K blocks (booths 61 and 65), with more than 150 voters registered before a panel of advocates Nayantara Roy and Sumita Hazarika and activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri. The audit covered 258 households over seven days. The Indian Express ('Voter for a decade, now, not on SIR draft rolls') also names the same four organisers, says the hearing was on Sunday at a baraat ghar in Jamia Nagar, and gives the audit as 1,579 voters in 307 households, conducted 9 to 16 October. So the date now rests on three sources, and the household count differs between them. The organiser field no longer needs 'as reported' and NFIW belongs in it without qualification.

fix.note: The Wire, live 11 September 2026. The text gives 5 September for the hearing. A screengrab caption in the same article dates the people's audit itself, not the hearing, to 9 September, and adds the National Federation of Indian Women among the groups. Read 22 October 2026.

checked.note: Opened The Wire (curl, 200). The text says verbatim 'The findings were presented at a public hearing, or Jan Sunwai, held in Mangolpuri on September 5, 2026.' and names the audit 'under the banner of Jan Sarokar, Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS) and Voter Adhikar Manch'. The caption, repeated twice, reads 'Screengrab from a people's audit of the Special Intensive Revision conduted by Jan Sarokar, Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, National Federation of Indian Women, Voter Adhikar Manch and other civil society organisations on September 9, 2026, Mangol Puri, Delhi. Credit: Facebook/@mazdoorkisaan'. So the caption dates the audit, not the hearing, and the two dates conflict only loosely. The article says the audit took more than three weeks, which a hearing on 5 September would have to follow. The page says it went live on 11 September 2026. The audit covered Mangolpuri Y-Block, eight polling booths and nearly 10,000 voters, so 'door-to-door audit of Y Block' in what is supported. Date 5 September is kept on the text. The MKSS Facebook post was not opened.
